Here is a concise, complete 12-week plan summary that integrates all prior adjustments: anti-inflammatory nutrition, aerobic/base cardio, a metabolic conditioning HIIT day, a plyometric day (with safeguards), and a Phase-2 intensity push, plus the option for a 1RM testing window at the end of Phase 3 if desired. The plan is organized week-by-week with the core structure, main lifts, accessories, cardio, and compliance notes. Dates assume a 2026-06-01 start.

Global guidelines (applies all weeks)
- Frequency: 4 training days per week (A, B, C, D). On-flow/flare days: substitute with light mobility, breathwork, and pelvic-floor–friendly core work.
- Session structure: 5–10 minute warm-up; main lifts 3–4 sets; accessory/core; 5–10 minute cool-down; RPE targets per day.
- Intensity: Phase 1 steady build; Phase 2 push in intensity with tempo; Phase 3 solidify strength with hypertrophy tempo variations; Phase 4 maintenance/deload as needed.
- Low-impact approach on flare days: avoid HIIT, heavy Valsalva, and jumping.

Phases at a glance
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Foundation and symptom-aware conditioning; establish routine; introduce low-impact resistance and mobility.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Stability, movement quality, and increased intensity with tempo; add one plyometric day on non-flare days and a HIIT/MetCon day on non-flare days.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9): Strength continue; begin controlled hypertrophy tempo; introduce 1RM testing window at end if desired; maintain fatigue management; aerobic base solidification.
- Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12): Consolidation, maintenance, deload around flare windows; refine onset times, recovery, and long-term maintenance plan.

Week-by-week plan

Week 1 (2026-06-01 to 2026-06-07)
- Day A – Upper body strength (pressing emphasis)
  - Warm-up: 5–7 min light cardio + activation
  - Incline push-ups or push-ups to bench: 3x8–10
  - Dumbbell bench press or floor press: 3x10
  - Dumbbell row or cable row: 3x10
  - Dumbbell shoulder press: 3x10
  - Pallof press: 3x10 per side
  - Core: dead bug 3x8 per side; diaphragmatic breathing 5 min
  - Cool-down: 5–7 min stretching
- Day B – Lower body strength
  - Warm-up: 5–7 min cardio + hip mobility
  - Goblet squat: 3x10
  - Romanian deadlift (moderate): 3x10
  - Glute bridge/hip thrust (light): 3x12
  - Split squats or step-ups: 3x8 per leg
  - Plank variations: 3x20–30s
  - Core/pelvic floor activation: 3x20s holds
- Day C – Mobility + light cardio
  - 20–30 min walking + mobility (hips, thoracic spine)
  - Breathing work 5–10 min
- Day D – Optional light cardio or rest
  - 15–20 min cycling or brisk walk if feeling good
- Cardio baseline: 3 days/week of 20–30 min easy cardio on non-flare days; on-flow days keep to 15–20 min very light movement if needed
- Plyometric day: none in Week 1

Week 2
- Day A: Upper body strength with +1 set or +2 reps (4x8–10)
- Day B: Lower body strength with tempo control (e.g., 2s down)
- Day C: Mobility/conditioning 30–35 min
- Day D: Core work and pelvic floor activation
- Cardio: add 1 light cardio day if energy allows (total 3–4 cardio days)

Week 3
- Progression: small load/reps increase; keep on-flow/flare restrictions; emphasize breath cues
- Maintain four days of training; cardio remains 20–40 minutes on non-flare days
- End of Phase 1 readiness check: ensure technique is solid and symptoms are well managed

Week 4 (Phase 2 starts)
- Phase 2 focus: intensification with tempo and additional set; start plyometric day on non-flare days
- Day A – Upper body strength + tempo
  - Incline push-up or push-up to bench: 4x8–10 (increase volume)
  - Dumbbell bench press/floor press: 4x8–10 with 2–3s eccentric
  - Bent-over row or cable row: 4x8–12
  - Dumbbell shoulder press: 3x8–12
  - Pallof press: 3x10 per side
  - Core/pelvic floor: 3 rounds (dead bug 8–12 reps per side)
- Day B – Lower body strength
  - Goblet squat or front goblet: 4x8–12
  - Romanian deadlift: 4x8–12 (tempo 2–0–1–0)
  - Hip thrust: 3x10–12
  - Bulgarian split squat: 3x8 per leg
  - Calf raises: 3x12–15
- Day C – Mobility + cardio (steady-state)
  - 25–35 min easy-to-moderate cardio
- Day D – HIIT MetCon (non-flare day)
  - 5–7 rounds of 20–25s high-intensity, 75s rest; bike/elliptical/rower

  - Post-HIIT core: 5–10 min gentle work; diaphragmatic breathing

- Plyometric Day (new) – non-flare day

  - Circuit (3 rounds to start)

    - Squat to overhead reach or small squat jump (1–2 inches) if tolerated: 6–8 reps
    - Split squat hops (low height) or split squat toe taps: 6 reps per leg
    - Marching bound with short step: 8–10 reps total
    - Core: 2 rounds of dead bug 8–12 reps
  - Cool-down: 5–8 min mobility
- Day D Continuation: Core and breathwork

Week 5 (Phase 2)
- Day A – Upper body strength + tempo progression
  - Push-ups: 4x8–10

  - Bent-over row: 4x8–12
  - Dumbbell lateral raise: 3x10–12
  - Pallof press: 3x10 per side
- Day B – Lower body + tempo
  - Front goblet squat: 4x8–12 with pause
  - Romanian deadlift: 4x8–12
  - Hip thrust/glute bridge: 3x10–12
  - Step-ups or reverse lunges: 3x8 per leg
  - Calf raises: 3x12–15
- Day C – Mobility + cardio
  - 30–40 min steady cardio
- Day D – Core stability
  - Pallof press: 3x12 per side
  - Dead bug with hold: 3x8 per side
  - Bird dog: 3x10 per side
- Plyometric Day: maintain 3 rounds if well tolerated; adjust height or reps as needed
- HIIT Day: continue if well tolerated; otherwise substitute with extra steady-state cardio

Week 6 (Phase 2 deload)
- Reduce total sets by 20–30% from Weeks 4–5; maintain tempo and control
- Optional light cardio 20–30 min
- Focus on form, breathing, pelvic floor, and symptom monitoring

Week 7 (Phase 3 begins)
- Phase 3 goals: strength with controlled hypertrophy tempo; introduce modest progression in volume and complexity; prep for potential 1RM testing at end of Phase 3
- Day A – Upper body strength + stability
  - 4x6–8 presses or push variations
  - Rows 4x8–10
  - Dumbbell pullovers or anti-rotation
  - Core 2–3 sets of 8–12
- Day B – Lower body strength
  - Front RDLs: 3–4x8–10
  - Bulgarian split squat: 3–4x8 per leg
  - Hip thrust/glute bridge: 3–4x10–12
  - Calf raises: 3x12–15
- Day C – Conditioning/low impact cardio
  - 25–35 min steady-state cardio (cycle/elliptical)
- Day D – Mobility + core
  - Mobility flow 20–30 min
  - Core sequence with pelvic floor activation: 15–20 min
- Optional: add one additional plyometric or MetCon day only if well tolerated and symptoms stable (but not during flare/on-flow)

Week 8 (Phase 3)
- Progressions: add slight weight or rep increases; incorporate tempo (2–0–1–0) on key lifts
- Keep HIIT/plyo days on non-flare days if tolerated; otherwise reduce or swap to steady-state cardio
- Ensure proper recovery and sleep

Week 9 (Phase 3 conclusion / potential 1RM testing window)
- Testing window option: Begin a safe 1RM testing protocol at end of Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9) if symptoms stable and client desires
  - Tests: 2–3 core lifts (e.g., goblet squat or barbell back squat if available, bench/press floor press, Romanian deadlift or hip hinge)
  - Protocol: warm-up sets, 1RM-estimate testing with submaximal attempts; avoid Valsalva; stop if pelvic floor strain or pain
- If not testing: continue progression with loads and reps
- Day C – Cardio: maintain 25–40 min steady-state
- Day D – Core stability and mobility: keep bracing with diaphragmatic breathing

Week 10 (Phase 4 start – consolidation)
- Phase 4 goals: maintenance and deload around flare windows; maintain gains; plan for ongoing routine
- Day A – Full-body strength circuit (4 rounds)
  - Goblet squat 8–12
  - Bench/incline press 8–12
  - Row 8–12
  - Hip thrust 8–12
  - Pallof press 8–10 per side
  - Core: dead bug 12 reps per side
- Day B – Posterior chain + hip mobility
  - Romanian deadlift 3–4x8–12
  - Glute bridge/hip thrust 3x12
  - Single-leg Romanian deadlift (light) 3x8 per leg
  - Glute activation work
- Day C – Low-impact cardio + mobility
  - 30–40 min walk or cycle easy pace
  - Full-body mobility flow
- Day D – Pelvic floor and breathwork
  - 3 rounds: 30s plank variations; 10 slow deep breaths
  - 5–10 min pelvic floor activation routine

Week 11
- Similar to Week 10 but reduce volume slightly if approaching any flare risk
- Focus on recovery, sleep, nutrition adherence, and symptom monitoring
- Optional lighter cardio or restorative activities if fatigue is high

Week 12 (Deload/maintenance finish)
- 2 days resistance training with light weights (or replace with mobility-only days)
- 1–2 days of light cardio or active recovery (20–30 min)
- Final check-in: review progress, symptom pattern, and plan for ongoing maintenance

Notes on 1RM testing (end of Phase 3)
- If you opt to perform a 1RM test, schedule on Weeks 7–9 only if symptoms are stable, fatigue is manageable, and there’s clinician clearance if needed.
- Use conservative testing: warm-up, 3–5 submaximal singles to ramp up, then attempt a safe near-max load with perfect technique; stop before technical failure if form deteriorates or pelvic floor strain occurs.
- If 1RM testing is completed, use the results to calibrate Phase 4 loads:
  - Use percentages based on tested 1RM (e.g., 65–75% for hypertrophy blocks, 75–85% for strength blocks)
  - Re-test every 6–8 weeks or as symptoms allow

Workout modality notes by day type
- On-flow/flare days: substitute with light mobility, diaphragmatic breathing, pelvic floor activation, and gentle walks; avoid HIIT, heavy Valsalva, and jumping.
- Non-flare days: standard resistance, plyometrics, HIIT, and cardio as outlined.
- Plyometrics: keep low-height, controlled landings; avoid jumping on on-flow/flare days.
- HIIT/MetCon: limited to non-flare days; keep total work time modest (8–12 minutes), priority is safe, controlled breathing and non-jarring movements.
- Cardio modalities: cycling, elliptical, brisk walking, swimming preferred for low impact; avoid high-impact running during symptom-prone periods.

Nutrition integration (recap)
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day
- Fat: 25–35% of calories, focus on unsaturated fats
- Carbs: balance to training load; emphasize complex carbs and fiber
- Anti-inflammatory staples: fatty fish, leafy greens, berries, olive oil, whole grains, legumes, nuts/seeds
- Iron considerations: pair iron sources with vitamin C when appropriate; monitor ferritin if symptomatic
- Hydration: 2.2–3 L/day, adjust for exercise and climate
- On flare days: smaller, more frequent meals; easier-to-d digest proteins; hydration and electrolytes as needed

Recovery and support
- Sleep: 7–9 hours nightly
- Recovery tools: light foam rolling, mobility work, breathwork, mindfulness
- Stress management: short daily activity such as walking, gentle yoga, or breathing routines
- Symptom monitoring: ongoing log of pain, GI symptoms, fatigue, menstrual cycle cues
- Medical coordination: maintain clinician/therapist updates; adjust plan per medical guidance
